traced_rule: An input is traced when the flight's own record states it: here RocketPy's example notebook, which holds the team's inputs. What no RocketPy example records is a placeholder in the designs built from them, the seven compared flights' too, and doesn't count against the tag: the surface finish, the rail buttons' size, and the fins' thickness and edge shape where no airfoil file or published section gives them. They move the drag, so a traced flight's inputs are stated, not exact. A flight is tagged not traced when its record leaves out, or contradicts, something else that moves the apogee.

flights.title: Astra, Faraday Rocketry UPV, EuRoC 2022 (L1350)
flights.source: astra_flight_sim.ipynb:123-131 (site, date), :247-280 (rocket, rail buttons, motor position, nose, fins), :316-318 (rail)
flights.motor_source: astra_flight_sim.ipynb:155-157: RocketPy's copy of the certified curve, cut at the notebook's burn time
flights.mass_source: astra_flight_sim.ipynb:249-251 (mass, inertia and center without the motor), :158-162 (the grain, whose density and size give the propellant), :168-170 (no motor dry mass or inertia)
flights.reference_rule: the highest reading of the log's `alt` column, in meters, the log read whole
flights.altimeter_evidence: the notebook calls it a COTS altimeter's flight (astra_flight_sim.ipynb:383-385), one row a second beside a latitude and a longitude, and records no more: barometric assumed, as hobby altimeters are

flights.title: Andromeda, Aristotle Space and Aeronautics Team, EuRoC 2022 (the team's curve)
flights.source: andromeda_flight_sim.ipynb:123-131 (site, date), :244-277 (rocket, rail buttons, motor position, nose, fins), :388-390 (rail)
flights.motor: the team's thrust file, flown in the notebook under the name of a Cesaroni M2020
flights.motor_source: andromeda_flight_sim.ipynb:153 and :162-165: "obtained by the team, after testing", cut at the notebook's burn time; the catalog file is commented out at :163
flights.mass_source: andromeda_flight_sim.ipynb:246-248 (mass, inertia and center without the motor), :166-170 (the grain), :176-178 (no motor dry mass or inertia)
flights.reference_rule: the highest reading of the log's `alt(m)` column, the log read whole
flights.altimeter_evidence: the notebook calls it a COTS altimeter (andromeda_flight_sim.ipynb:459-461), logged in feet with a vertical speed, and records no more: barometric assumed, as hobby altimeters are
untraced: the flight carried the team's air brakes, and no record says when or how far they opened: none is flown here, so any opening leaves this prediction high
the thrust file holds more impulse than the Cesaroni M2020 reload it is named for is certified at, so the notebook does not settle which motor the logged flight burned

catalog_curve.why: the reload the notebook names, on its certified curve as bundled, whole. Shown beside the counted prediction and never counted: every RocketPy flight here is counted on its example's own thrust file

flights.note: both tags are the research note's findings (docs/research/andromeda-impulse.md), written down before this flight was flown
